editorial.headline: Sharia Re-Guarantee: Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A specialist Sharia activity open across all stated business scales, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
This activity is Sharia re-guarantee business: providing guarantees for the fulfilment of the financial obligations of Sharia guarantee companies. It is conducted wholly under Sharia principles. The scope is deliberately focused: the activity sits in the financial assurance surrounding Sharia guarantee companies, rather than describing a broad, general-purpose guarantee operation.

Registration is open at every stated business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth is significant because the record does not reserve the activity for one size of enterprise. A business may therefore be established within any of those listed scales, while remaining within the same core scope: Sharia-based re-guarantees supporting the financial obligations of Sharia guarantee companies.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. Its foreign-investment position is recorded under Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021, and there is no lower ownership cap stated for this activity.

Bali does not present a hidden prohibition here. The province-wide, permanent moratorium blocks foreign-investment registrations for activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk. This activity is not blocked by that rule: at the Large scale, its OSS risk assessment is Medium-High or High. Bali therefore marks it as acceptable or higher-risk rather than blocked, so a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today. The national position and the Bali position point in the same practical direction: full foreign ownership is permitted nationally, and Bali's moratorium does not prevent registration for this activity.
